name: El Sabino de San Juan

location.address: Plazuela de San Juan Bautista, Calle Plazuela San Juan, Barrio San Juan (Colonia Xacalco), Xochimilco, CP 16000

verified_sources: https://proyectos.sedema.cdmx.gob.mx/arbolespatrimoniales/arboles.html (KML placemark 7, SEDEMA official Arboles Patrimoniales register, coordinates + species + circumference)
access: Free, standing in a public plazuela (small plaza) in the barrio of San Juan, open at all times.
transport: In central Xochimilico, within walking distance (roughly 1-1.5 km) of the Xochimilico historic centre and the Tren Ligero Xochimilico terminus; exact walk time not independently confirmed.
verify_notes: SEDEMA's official 'Arboles Patrimoniales' register (KML, Aug 2025 gazette-backed declaration) lists this ahuehuete at Plazuela San Juan Bautista, Xochimilico: total height recorded as 24.5 m (matches an independently found figure of '24.5 metros' for this same tree elsewhere), trunk diameter (DAP) 590 cm, circumference 1853.544 cm -> girth_cm rounded to 1854. That girth is unusually large for the city's other patrimonial ahuehuetes (next-largest here is ~1382 cm), so treat it as a single-source figure pending a second measurement. Age: local legend (chronicler Rodolfo Cordero Lopez) holds it was planted by Cuauhtemoc in 1521 in gratitude to the Xochimilca people; this is a story, not a documented planting date, so age_estimate is left broad and the 500-year figure is reported as legend, never sharpened. IMPORTANT CAUTION FOR ALIVE-NOW CHECK: multiple news sources (Excelsior, El Universal, Lopez Doriga) report that in September 2018 this same tree ('El Sabino', ~500 years old, Plazuela San Juan Bautista) partially collapsed/broke in strong winds after specialists from Universidad de Chapingo had flagged inadequate maintenance a year earlier. However, SEDEMA's own Arboles Patrimoniales register was compiled and the tree measured/declared in 2025, seven years after that event, which is strong evidence a living remainder still stands and was assessed as 'Buena' or similar recent condition (full condition field was truncated in the fetched KML text and should be re-checked). Delivered flagged rather than confidently 'alive and undamaged' because the 2018 collapse is real and its long-term aftermath (full tree vs. surviving portion) was not independently re-confirmed by a post-2018 photo or article in this pass; the writer should say plainly that the tree lost part of its structure in 2018 and note it stands today per the 2025 official register.

name: El Viejo del Agua (Ahuehuete de Santa Catarina)
age_estimate: roughly 700 years (city's own estimate, basis not published)

location.address: Prolongacion Tlatenco 20, Colonia Santa Catarina, Azcapotzalco, CP 02250 (behind the Escuela Primaria Sotero Prieto, next to the Parroquia de Santa Catarina Martir)

verified_sources: https://proyectos.sedema.cdmx.gob.mx/arbolespatrimoniales/arboles.html (KML placemark 6, SEDEMA official Arboles Patrimoniales register)
access: Free, standing beside the Santa Catarina Martir parish/plaza in the historic barrio; publicly visible year round.
transport: In the Barrio de Santa Catarina, Azcapotzalco; nearest Metro is Camarones (Linea 7) or El Rosario area, roughly 2 km away. Exact walk time not independently confirmed.
verify_notes: Named 'El Viejo del Agua' (ahuehuete = Nahuatl for 'old one of the water') on 27-28 June 2025 by Mexico City's Head of Government Clara Brugada, the first tree declared under the new 'Arboles Patrimoniales' programme, timed to the 700th anniversary of the founding of Tenochtitlan. Multiple outlets (Infobae, the Jefatura de Gobierno's own press release, Publimetro) independently report the '700 years' figure but none states how it was derived (no growth-rate or ring-count method given) -- treat as a claim repeated at face value, not a derived estimate, hence the broad 500-700 band rather than a sharp 700. SEDEMA's own register gives circumference 1382.30 cm (girth_cm 1382) and total height recorded as '2700' in the source KML, which is almost certainly 27.00 m with the decimal stripped (the same register has several other height fields that read as physically impossible four-digit numbers, e.g. 2200, 2750, 2800, all of which resolve to sane 22-28 m figures once divided by 100; flagging this as a register data-quality issue for future passes). Stands behind a primary school and beside the parish church; described in press coverage as a living witness the community rallied around, consistent with being alive and in good condition as of the June 2025 declaration.

Its rescue-from-felling story and the sidewalk-corner setting (readable trunk and crown from the street) make it a strong collectible point independent of the age question.
